rebase_note: Re-measured after the orchestrator rebased this branch onto da6d05b (PR #71 merged out of queue and flipped PRs #66-#70 to CONFLICTING). Both suites re-run rather than arithmetic adjusted by hand; the 85-case republish survived the rebase unchanged. CORRECTED 2026-08-28 by PR #69 R7 — the two ledger claims this note originally made were FALSE, and they are restated here rather than quietly edited out. It claimed 'zero rows present in origin/main are missing from the branch' and that 'a literal de-duplication by ts would have destroyed one of each [duplicate-ts pair], and did not'. Both were wrong: the conflict resolution used across four rebases DID deduplicate by ts, and origin/main legitimately holds duplicate-ts rows (distinct runs sharing a timestamp), so exactly one of each pair was destroyed — 11 rows, at ts 20260821-214528, 20260822-111646, 20260822-161720, 20260822-174202, 20260822-234414, 20260822-235019, 20260823-164337, 20260823-212444, 20260823-215850, 20260823-232059, 20260824-013503. Collateral worth naming: 20260822-174202 is the row T-M39-15-D3 cites as 'the single exception' in its own 44-null-cost / 43-sub-3s arithmetic, so the PR had deleted the evidence its own debt block cites. Why the original check missed it: it compared SETS of row bodies, which cannot see a multiplicity going from 2 to 1 — the same shape as the id-collision class this PR exists for, one level down. The orchestrator repaired evals/report/history.jsonl in commit 33dbf42; the implementer re-verified with a MULTISET comparison rather than the set comparison that produced the false claim: 2192 rows on origin/main, 0 missing from the branch by multiplicity, and 20260822-174202 present twice again.

resolutions.covered_by: task-id-parse-boundary (new, invariant) — 5 fixtures: true duplicate TODO id, true duplicate DONE id + open-and-done, prose near-miss, fenced near-miss, and this repo's id vocabulary
resolutions.watched_red: evals/report/20260827-204821-invariant.json, before the fix, with the old ^### (\S+) —  extraction: fixture 3 {'want': {}, 'got': {'duplicate_todo_ids': ['Reopen'], 'duplicate_done_ids': ['Standing']}} and fixture 4 {'want': {}, 'got': {'duplicate_todo_ids': ['M43']}}. Fixtures 1, 2 and 5 passed in that same run, which is the shape that mattered: the probe was catching real collisions AND inventing false ones, and only the second half was invisible.
resolutions.fix: _TASK_ID = [A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)* plus stripping fenced blocks, with the extraction moved into _task_ids(text, marker) — the refactor is what makes the boundary gradeable against fixtures at all, which is the root of the finding rather than the regex.
resolutions.deviation_from_instruction: The finding proposed reusing the groundwork pr-loop ready.py ID pattern as the repo's own precedent. REJECTED as a literal reuse, and measured before rejecting: that pattern is [A-Z]+\d+, which matches M43 but none of T-M39-15, M45-D9, T-RANK-MIRROR or T-ADR-NUM, and applied to this tree's TODO.md it finds 18 of the 188 task headings. Adopting it would have blinded the probe to most of the id space it exists to guard — a far worse defect than the one being repaired. The SHAPE is borrowed (an id is a typed token, not 'anything before the em dash'); the vocabulary is this repo's, and fixture 5 pins the forms so a later narrowing cannot quietly drop one. The finding's claim that ready.py 'finds 188 tasks' does not hold.
resolutions.non_vacuity: Fixtures 1 and 2 are the positive control: they stay RED-worthy (they assert the probe still reports duplicate_todo_ids, duplicate_done_ids and in_todo_and_done), so a fix that simply stopped extracting ids would fail them.

retraction_handled: The orchestrator retracted a claim it had given for D3 — that PR #71's rows are 'dirty and superseded regardless under T-M39-13's citable rule' — after re-deriving it. The implementer had already committed that sentence in 2c2df76 and confirmed the retraction independently against origin/main before amending: of the 73 sub-0.9 rows, 19 are dirty:false and therefore citable by construction, so the claim was false. D3 now argues the stronger and true version — the population is inert by COINCIDENCE (every such row sits at a case count nothing publishes: the 19 clean ones at 5, 6, 10, 18, 20, 22, 32, 49, 53, 63, 96, against a live 85/229), not by any rule, so revisiting a count makes them citable again and the ADR-019 amendment adds no admission control. The implementer added one figure of its own: 5 rows run under 3s WITH a real recorded cost, which is the independent reason the signature must be the conjunction rather than the wall-clock half alone.
